mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to wage inflation and increased production costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates growing demand, which boosts economic activity and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST is increasing.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a contraction in supply, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO MoM < 0%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when PAYEMS MoM > 0% and UNRATE MoM < 0%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real final sales (RSAFS) signals weakening demand, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when RSAFS MoM < 0%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) indicates strong economic growth, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when GDPC1 is increasing.
